version: "2.1"
source: payments
owner: keel-servicing
description: Daily payment activity posted by Keel Servicing, Harbor Lending's loan servicer.
delivery:
  directory: landing/payments
  file_pattern: "keel_payments_{yyyymmdd}.csv"
  redelivery_pattern: "keel_payments_{yyyymmdd}_r{n}.csv"
  schedule: business_days
  due_by: "05:00 on the calendar day after the business day"
  holidays: >-
    No file is delivered for bank holidays on the Harbor business calendar. Payments
    received on a holiday are included in the next business day's file.
  redelivery: >-
    A corrected or complete file is re-sent with an _r<n> suffix. The highest revision
    supersedes earlier ones for the same business day.
format:
  type: csv
  header: true
  trailer: "TRL|<record_count>|<control_total>, control_total = sum of amount over all records"
columns:
  - {name: payment_id, type: varchar, required: true}
  - {name: loan_id, type: varchar, required: true}
  - {name: payment_date, type: date, required: true}
  - {name: amount, type: "decimal(18,2)", required: true, unit: "US dollars, two decimal places"}
  - {name: principal_amount, type: "decimal(18,2)", required: true, unit: "US dollars, two decimal places"}
  - {name: interest_amount, type: "decimal(18,2)", required: true, unit: "US dollars, two decimal places"}
  - {name: cdc_op, type: varchar, required: true, description: "I = new payment, U = correction"}
  - {name: cdc_seq, type: integer, required: true}
semantics:
  cdc: >-
    Each record is a change event. The record with the highest cdc_seq for a payment_id is
    the current state. After a connector restart events can be sent again; a re-sent
    event keeps its original cdc_seq.
  expected_values: "A single payment above 50000.00 dollars is exceptional."
change_policy:
  notice_days: 30
  notice_to: data-platform@harborlending.example
  breaking_changes: column renames or removals, type changes, unit changes, file naming changes
  on_breach: >-
    Do not adapt the pipeline to an unannounced breaking change. Raise it with the vendor
    through the owner contact so the vendor corrects and re-sends the file.
"}}

content.text: Quick confirmation in the warehouse that loaded values match the file (not an ingestion bug):

input.sql: select payment_date, count(*), sum(amount), max(amount), avg(amount) from raw.payments where payment_date >= '2026-10-28' group by 1 order by 1

input.reason: keel_payments_20261102.csv amounts delivered in cents rather than dollars (unannounced unit change; sum 32,576,379.00 vs trailer 325,763.79, 100x). Awaiting corrected _r1 file from Keel.

input.summary: keel_payments_20261102.csv (business day 2026-11-02, arrived 2026-11-03 03:38) has amount, principal_amount and interest_amount in cents, not dollars as contract keel_payments v2.1 requires ("US dollars, two decimal places"). Example: P000014890 amount 382651.00. The 260 records add up to 32,576,379.00, but the trailer says TRL|260|325763.79, so the values are 100x too high. This is an unannounced unit change, which breaches the contract. We have quarantined the partition on our side. Please re-send a corrected file as keel_payments_20261102_r1.csv with amounts in dollars, and confirm future files will not be affected. Please cc vendor-management@harborlending.example.

evidence: ALR-A4719D: loaded sum 32,576,379.00 vs trailer 325,763.79 (100x) for 260 records
landing/payments/keel_payments_20261102.csv: amounts in cents (e.g. 382651.00) vs 20261030 file in dollars (3332.27)
raw.payments query: max amount 421127.00 on 2026-11-02 vs ~4,300 on prior days; contract says >50,000 is exceptional and units are US dollars
ALR-D529F2: negative balances caused by inflated payments; ALR-7993D8 dbt_build tr-000245/tr-000246 failed on that test; ALR-94240C mart stale as a result
No pipeline commits since 2026-08-26; no Keel announcement of a format change; no _r1 redelivery yet
input.summary: Keel Servicing sent the 2026-11-02 payments file with amounts in cents, not dollars. The trailer total is still in dollars, so the loaded total is 100x the trailer. The inflated payments pushed loan balances below zero, which failed the dbt test, so dbt_build failed and mart_delinquency went stale. I quarantined raw.payments 2026-11-02, and the rebuild and publish then succeeded. I escalated to Keel and asked for a corrected _r1 file. Per the contract, I did not change the pipeline to handle the unit change.
